benchmarks.unscheduled_downtime: Under 3.0% (Exceeding 5% creates severe production schedule cascading delays)
benchmarks.anomaly_tolerance: 0.8% - 2.0% (Industrial anomalies indicate vibration harmonics, thermal breakdown, or sensor telemetry drift)

knowledge_chunks.text: World-class manufacturing environments target Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) at 85% or higher, combining 90% Availability, 95% Performance, and 99.9% Quality. In logistics and distribution, On-Time In-Full (OTIF) delivery must remain above 95% to maintain supplier tier status and avoid penalty deductions.

Manufacturing outliers indicate physical hardware degradation: (1) Bearing or Motor Friction causing abnormal vibration or thermal spikes, (2) Sensor Drift sending erroneous baseline telemetry, or (3) Raw Material Batch Inconsistencies causing sudden bursts of dimensional defect rejections.

Machine operating speed correlates directly with throughput, but exhibits an exponential non-linear threshold where increased speed degrades quality yield. When ambient temperature and vibration correlate strongly with defect counts, thermal expansion in mechanical fixtures is the direct root cause.

Priority Manufacturing Reliability Plan: (1) Implement vibration and temperature threshold telemetry for condition-based predictive maintenance before mechanical failure occurs; (2) Rebalance assembly line bottlenecks based on takt time analysis; (3) Audit supplier raw material certifications on defect-correlated production batches.
